sentences.text:
As per the allegations made in the FIR, the first informant, namely, Rajeshkumar Dahyabhai Patel,
had initially submitted an application before Navrangpura Police Station on 03.01.2020, pursuant to which his statement was recorded and an inquiry was initiated, culminating in registration of the FIR.
It is alleged that the complainant's daughter, namely Krupal, had completed her nursing course and intended to pursue further studies in Canada.
It is alleged that the complainant came into contact with an entity known as "Om Education", which was engaged in providing services relating to foreign visas and admissions.
Accused No.1 is stated to be the proprietor, accused No.2 the manager, and accused No.3, i.e., the present applicant, an office bearer of the said entity.

In the month of January 2019, the complainant visited the office of Om Education, where all the accused introduced themselves and represented that they were engaged in the business of visa processing and foreign admissions.

Upon inquiry regarding admission and visa formalities for Canada, the complainant was informed that the total expenses would be Rs.16,50,000/-, along with Rs.20,000/-
towards consultation charges.

On 26.01.2019, the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined complainant, along with his daughter, visited the office and paid Rs.20,000/- towards consultation charges, for which a receipt was issued.
Thereafter, Rs.5,000/- was collected on two occasions towards application charges, followed by a demand of Rs.49,000/- towards visa processing fees.

2.1 It is further alleged that on 30.02.2019, the complainant again visited the office and paid Rs.49,000/-, for which a receipt was issued on a blank paper by one Darshitbhai, and an offer letter from a college was shown.
Subsequently, the complainant was informed that the admission had been secured and that Rs.15,40,000/- was required towards admission fees.
Two cheques of Rs.7,70,000/- each were issued on 04.03.2019 drawn on SBI Bank
however, one cheque was returned on the ground of signature mismatch, and another cheque issued in lieu thereof was subsequently cleared.
Despite demands, no formal receipt was issued, and assurances were given that the same would be provided later.
2.2 It is further alleged that the complainant and his daughter were called for biometric fingerprinting, for which they attended and receipts were issued.
However, by September 2019, no visa had been NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined received.
Upon inquiry at the office of Om Education on 25.11.2019, the complainant was informed that the visa had been rejected on 20.08.2019.
On further inquiry with the immigration authorities in Canada, it was revealed that the visa application had been rejected due to non-payment of requisite fees and inadequate documentation.

Thereafter, the complainant approached the office of Om Education seeking refund of the amount, which was refused by the accused persons, who instead directed him to recover the same from the college.
Upon inquiry with Humber College as well as Scotia Bank, it was revealed that no such payments had been made by the accused persons.

sentences.text: On the basis of the aforesaid allegations, the impugned FIR came to be lodged, which is the subject matter of challenge before this Court at the instance of the present applicant - original accused No.3.
3 Heard the learned advocate Mr. Ashish Dagli for the applicant and learned advocate Mr. Vivek Bhamare for the respondent No.2 and learned APP Ms. Vrunda Shah for the respondent-State.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined 4

Learned advocate Mr. Ashish Dagli appearing for the applicant submits that accused No.1 was carrying on business in the name of "Om Tours and Travels" and had himself lodged a complaint against accused No.2 alleging that he had been cheated by the said accused.

It is further submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Dagli that both "Om Education" and "Om Tours and Travels" are operating from the same premises, and that Om Education has been functioning for the past six to seven years.

It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Dagli that Om Education maintains a Bank Account with Indian Bank and that the present applicant was merely employed as an operator,
having no role in the day-to-day affairs of the firm, nor any authority to collect money.
It is further submitted that the applicant is a salaried employee drawing a monthly salary of Rs.15,000/-, which itself had not been paid for the preceding two months.

4.1 Learned advocate Mr. Dagli further submits that the applicant is unmarried and has been suffering from serious ailments, for which he underwent prolonged medical treatment, including hospitalization for about 30 days and thereafter being bedridden for nearly three years.

After partial recovery, he secured employment with Om Education on reference, primarily as a phone NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined operator, in order to meet the substantial medical expenses incurred by him, stated to be in the range of Rs.25 to 30 lakhs.

It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Dagli that the applicant, acting under the instructions of accused Nos.1 and 2, had merely contacted the first informant once for biometric formalities and thereafter conveyed that the visa application was under process.
It is contended that the applicant neither collected any amount nor issued or signed any receipts, and had no involvement in the alleged transactions.

In the aforesaid circumstances, it is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Dagli that the allegations made against the present applicant are wholly untenable and amount to a gross abuse and misuse of the process of law.
It is, therefore, prayed that the impugned FIR be quashed and set aside.
5 Per contra, learned APP Ms. Vrunda Shah has submitted that the investigation qua the present applicant is still in progress and that accused No.3 is absconding.
It is submitted by the learned APP Ms. Shah that, at this stage, examination of the defence put forth by the applicant, including his claim of being merely an employee, is impermissible.

In that background, it is prayed that the present application NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED:
01/04/2026 undefined be dismissed.

6 Learned advocate Mr. Vivek Bhamare appearing for respondent No.2-original complainant, in support of the submissions advanced by learned APP Ms. Shah, has further submitted that the present applicant himself was actively handling the affairs of Om Education and had directed the Akash Chandraprakash Gautam vs State Of Gujarat on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67527054/
3 complainant to deposit an amount of Rs.49,000/- for expediting the visa process.

sentences.text:
It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Bhamare that false and fabricated documents were shown to the first informant indicating that the admission of his daughter had been confirmed at Humber College,
Canada, whereas, in fact, no such process had been undertaken.

It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Bhamare that, at the instance of the present applicant, the first informant and his daughter underwent biometric formalities and that an amount of Rs.16,09,000/- deposited by the complainant was falsely represented to have been transferred to Scotia Bank towards tuition fees for Humber College, Canada, which, in reality, was neither deposited nor processed.

6.1 Learned advocate Mr. Bhamare has further submitted that when the visa process was getting delayed, the first informant along with his NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined daughter approached the office of Om Education,
wherein the applicant assured them that even if there was some delay in the visa process, the admission would not be rejected on any ground.

It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr.
Bhamare that, at the time when such assurance was given, the visa application had already been rejected, however, the complainant was misled to believe that both admission and visa would be secured.

6.2 It is submitted by the learned advocate Mr. Bhamare that, despite no steps having been taken for securing admission at Humber College, Canada, nor any tuition fees having been deposited with Scotia Bank, forged receipts and fabricated documents were shown to the complainant with a view to induce him.
It is, therefore, contended that the present applicant was actively involved in the commission of the alleged offences.

In the aforesaid background, it is submitted that the impugned FIR deserves to be taken to its logical conclusion by completion of investigation and, therefore, the present application deserves to be dismissed.

7 Considering the submissions advanced by the learned advocates for the respective parties, as well NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined as on perusal of the impugned FIR, the moot question that arises for consideration is whether the prosecution initiated against the present applicant can be said to be a sheer abuse of the process of law ?
8 To determine the above question the allegations which are made in the FIR is required to be tested.

8.1 The present applicant is arraigned as accused No.3 and is alleged to have been present at the office of Om Education along with accused Nos.1 and 2, where accused Nos.2 and 3 introduced themselves as office bearers of the said entity.
The first informant, along with his daughter, had approached the office of Om Education for securing admission at Humber College, Canada and for processing the visa.

It is alleged that an amount of Rs.16,09,000/- was collected by the accused persons and fake receipts indicating payment of GIC fees in Scotiabank, as well as receipts of Humber College, Canada, were shown to the complainant.

It is further alleged that the present applicant had informed the first informant on 02.09.2019 that even if there was a delay in the visa process, the admission would not be cancelled however, by that time, the visa application had Akash Chandraprakash Gautam vs State Of Gujarat on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67527054/
4 already been rejected on 20.08.2019, as per the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined information received from the immigration authorities, on account of non-payment of visa fees and submission of inadequate documents.

The contention of the applicant is that he was merely an employee acting under the instructions of accused Nos.1 and 2.
9

In the opinion of this Court, while exercising powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, it would not be appropriate to embark upon an inquiry as to whether the applicant was merely an employee or had actively participated in the commission of the alleged offence.
Such determination falls squarely within the domain of the learned trial Court.
It is not open to invoke the inherent jurisdiction of this Court by contending that, upon a reasonable appreciation of the evidence, the accusations would not be sustained.
The High Court cannot usurp the functions of the trial Court, and it is for the trial Court to adjudicate the matter in accordance with law and on the basis of the evidence led before it.
This Court cannot undertake an appraisal of evidence or examine whether the same is sufficient for conviction or acquittal.
Appreciation of evidence lies within the exclusive domain of the learned trial Court.

In that view of the matter, the defence raised by the present applicant that he was merely an employee acting under the instructions of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined
his employer is a matter to be considered by the trial Court at the appropriate stage while evaluating the evidence.

10 This Court has referred to the decision of the Apex Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal,
reported in 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, wherein the Apex Court has laid down the guidelines governing the exercise of inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which are reproduced hereinbelow:
"102.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we have given the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

(i) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined (ii) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any, accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Akash Chandraprakash Gautam vs State Of Gujarat on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67527054/
5 Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

entities.text: Akash Chandraprakash Gautam vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(iv) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(v) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(vi) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act,
providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.
(vii) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/11532/2020 JUDGMENT DATED: 01/04/2026 undefined 11

This Court does not find any merit falling under the criteria of the decision of the Bhajan Lal (supra)
therefore the application deserves to be dismissed.
12 Resultantly, this application is dismissed.
Rule is discharged.

Interim relief stands vacated,
forthwith.
